title: 0009 信使0010 城隍爷
content_zh:
洪涛回到公廨换好衣服，戴上幕笠，牵着两匹马傻愣愣的站在大门内，和正在值班的士卒大眼瞪小眼互望了一刻钟左右，才等到了典狱官。
他已经脱下官服，换了件青色长衫，头上也戴着幕笠，但品相比洪涛的高级多了。两人站在一起，妥妥的是一主一仆。
幕笠就是围了一圈面纱的斗笠，通常为男子佩戴，除了防雨防风沙，最重要的功能就是把相貌挡住。
如果是女人外出，则会换成一种叫幂笠的帽子。其实也是幕笠，就是面纱更长，能到腰部甚至膝盖处，把半身和全身都遮住。
镇妖殿对工作人员有严格规定，工作期间必须戴面甲，就是面具。由皮革制成，上面刻印了兽纹，故意弄得很吓人。
实际上这种面甲并没有太多保护作用，只是为了掩盖真实相貌，算作对工作人员的保护。毕竟干的都是不太讨人喜欢的工作，万一被记恨不清楚长相更难报复。
外出的时候也要求遮挡面容，一般以幕笠代替面甲。也有例外，比如南殿的校尉、玄鸟卫、青衣郎在外出执行抓捕任务时脸上都带着金属面甲，除了掩盖面容之外还能起到保护作用。
“还等什么？”典狱官刚要认镫上马，发现洪涛还傻愣愣的站着，看了看左右问。
“卑职以为大人要带着部曲……”洪涛尴尬的抿了抿嘴唇，赶紧爬上了马背。
“多事……驾！”典狱官面色如何看不到，可语气不太友好，上马就走，根本不看后面一眼。
“驾、驾驾……吁吁……大人等等卑职、大人等等……卑职不善马术……”洪涛本不想再张嘴，可架不住这匹马不让。一催就急加速，一缓就急刹车，好像不具备定速巡航功能。
还不敢表现出很会骑马甚至会驯马，那些能力与行刑力士的身份非常不相符，只好在后面一顿哀嚎，再弄得手忙脚乱些。
“吁……”对于这么个笨手笨脚的手下典狱官也没什么好办法，鲁王殿下有令，好歹也得安全送到城隍庙，然后再将一路上的点点滴滴全书面上报才算遵命。
至于说鲁王殿下为什么突然重视起这名行刑力士，是否还有其它深意，目前还摸不着头脑。所以尽管不怎么喜欢这个人和这趟差遣也得忍着，尽量不表露出太多情绪。
“洪涛，你到诏狱几年了？”
光忍着不发作不够，还得趁机摸摸底。于是作为上官就先说话了，从个人情况谈起，然后再去和北殿案牍库里的卷宗比对，看看能不能找出鲁王的意图。
“回大人，卑职16岁入诏狱，先从杂役做起，26岁升为行刑力士，至今已整整24年了。”这种无头无脑的交谈不光让典狱官别扭，洪涛更别扭，根本不知道该从何说起，只能字字斟酌尽可能不瞎编。
“24年……你师从何人？”要说这位典狱官也够不敬业的，居然对下属的情况如此无知，听了回答之后马上面露惊诧。
“卑职是家传，微末手段都来自亡父。”
“哦，原来如此……那你与鲁王殿下？”

家传手艺，姓洪，入职24年。有了这些关键词，典狱官就大概知道这位当了10年杂役之后又当了14年行刑力士，始终得不到升迁是怎么回事了。
原因极其复杂，按理说镇妖殿不归任何部门管辖，直接听命于皇帝，人际关系应该比较简单才对，然而实际情况正好相反。
朝堂里数得上号的势力都在想尽办法往镇妖殿里塞人，又做得非常隐秘，很难辨明谁是谁的眼线。可越是这样，互相之间的明争暗斗越激烈，无缘无故遭受打压的情况比比皆是。
content_en:
Hong Tao returned to the palace, changed his clothes, put on his curtains, led two horses and stood dumbly inside the gate, staring at each other with the soldiers on duty for about a quarter of an hour, before he waited for the warden.
He had taken off his official uniform and put on a blue gown. He also wore a curtain on his head, but his appearance was much higher than that of Hong Tao. The two of them stood together, as if they were one master and one servant.
A curtain is a bamboo hat with a veil around it. It is usually worn by men. In addition to protecting against rain and sand, its most important function is to block the appearance.
If a woman goes out, she will wear a hat called Mi Li. In fact, it is also a Mukasa, that is, the veil is longer and can reach the waist or even the knees, covering half of the body and the whole body.
The Demon Suppression Hall has strict regulations for its staff, and they must wear visors, that is, masks during work. Made of leather with animal prints engraved on it, it was intentionally scary.
In fact, this kind of mask does not have much protective effect. It is only used to cover up the true appearance and is regarded as the protection of the staff. After all, they are doing unflattering jobs, and if they are resented and don’t know their appearance, it will be even harder to take revenge.
You are also required to cover your face when going out, usually wearing a mask instead of a mask. There are exceptions. For example, the captain of the South Palace, the Black Bird Guards, and the Qing Yi Lang all wear metal masks on their faces when they go out to carry out arrest missions. In addition to covering their faces, they can also play a protective role.
"What are you waiting for?" The warden asked as he was about to put his stirrup on his horse and found Hong Tao still standing dumbfounded.
"I thought you were going to take me with you..." Hong Tao pursed his lips in embarrassment and quickly climbed onto the horse's back.
"Nothing... drive!" You couldn't see the expression on the warden's face, but his tone was not very friendly. He mounted his horse and left without even looking back.
"Drive, drive, drive... Xuxu... My lord, please wait for your humble position, my lord, please wait... Your humble position is not good at horsemanship..." Hong Tao didn't want to open his mouth again, but he couldn't hold back the horse. It accelerates sharply when pushed, and brakes sharply when slowed down. It seems that it does not have a cruise control function.
He didn't dare to show that he was good at riding horses or even taming horses. Those abilities were very inconsistent with his status as an executioner, so he had to wail behind him and get more confused.
"Uu..." There is no good way to deal with such a clumsy subordinate warden. His Royal Highness King Lu has an order, and he must be delivered to the City God's Temple safely, and then everything along the way must be reported in writing before he can comply with the order.
As for why His Royal Highness Prince Lu suddenly paid attention to this executioner, it is still unclear whether there is any other deeper meaning. So even though I didn't really like this person or this assignment, I had to endure it and try not to show too many emotions.
"Hong Tao, how many years have you been in prison?"
It's not enough to just endure it without having an attack, you have to take the opportunity to feel it out. So as a Shangguan, I spoke first, starting with my personal situation, and then compared it with the files in the North Hall's archives to see if I could find out King Lu's intentions.
"My lord, I was sent to prison at the age of 16 for a humble job. I started as a handyman and was promoted to an executioner at the age of 26. It has been 24 years now." This kind of mindless conversation not only made the warden awkward, but Hong Tao was even more awkward. He didn't know where to start, so he could only consider every word and try not to make it up.
"In 24 years...who did you study under?" This warden was quite unprofessional and ignorant of the situation of his subordinates. After hearing the answer, he immediately showed surprise.
"Humble positions are inherited from the family, and low-level means are all inherited from the late father."
"Oh, I see... Then you and His Highness Prince Lu?"
The craftsmanship is passed down from his family. His surname is Hong and he has been working for 24 years. With these keywords, the warden probably knew why this man, who had been a handyman for 10 years and then an executioner for 14 years, never got promoted.
The reason is extremely complex. It stands to reason that the Demon Suppression Palace is not under the jurisdiction of any department and directly takes orders from the emperor. The interpersonal relationship should be relatively simple. However, the actual situation is exactly the opposite.
ChaotangCountless forces are trying their best to smuggle people into the Demon Suppression Palace, and they are doing so in a very secretive manner, making it difficult to identify who is whose informant. But the more this happens, the more intense the overt and covert fights between each other become, and it is common for them to be suppressed for no reason.
